page: Microsoft Azure F80amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the Famdsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 80 dedicated physical cores and 80 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI. The server is equipped with 640.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core, and includes 9449 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the F80amds_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached bandwidth and large block uncached read/write bandwidth all ranking in the top 10%. This high-speed memory architecture is complemented by a PassMark memory score in the top 25%. Computational efficiency is further highlighted by top-tier results in gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and PassMark database operations.

The combination of dense memory allocation, high-capacity local NVMe SSD storage, and dedicated 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC cores makes this instance highly cost-efficient for resource-intensive workloads. It is optimized for large-scale database operations, as evidenced by its top-tier Redis SET performance of 196.41 million operations per second and high static web serving throughput. While it lacks a dedicated GPU, the system delivers strong performance in CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for medium-sized 7B models. It is well-suited for memory-intensive databases, data warehousing, heavy ETL pipelines, and high-throughput web serving.

The F80amds_v7 is optimized for large-scale databases, Redis deployments, high-throughput web serving, and complex data processing pipelines.
